summary: Maine Department of Education supports targeted improvements to E-Rate while preserving its core role in providing connectivity to schools and libraries. Maine Department of Education emphasizes preserving E-Rate funding to maintain connectivity and affordability, not using the program as a reason to end it, and supports coordination with other federal broadband programs. The comment supports coordination among federal broadband programs and appropriate safeguards against duplicative funding, while opposing the limitation or sunsetting of E-Rate. It emphasizes the importance of managed internal broadband services for small and rural school systems and the need to maintain a clear distinction between ensuring network safety and regulating classroom instruction. The comment also opposes conditioning E-Rate eligibility on student academic outcomes and screen-time li The comment argues against narrowing the eligibility scope of E-Rate to only specific equipment and services, which could limit access to broadband for schools and libraries. Maine supports continued efforts to strengthen program integrity, simplify administration, improve transparency, and ensure that E-Rate investments remain cost-effective.
